title: The Living Body
subtitle: Tap any colored word to explore it — red for Ayurveda, amber for physiology, olive for anatomy.

blocks.name: Chemical
blocks.info: This stage encompasses atoms and molecules, the tiny particles that are the fundamental components of all living organisms. A collection of atoms and molecules organizes to form a cell.

blocks.name: Cellular
blocks.info: A cell is composed of atoms and molecules and serves as the fundamental unit of life.

blocks.name: Tissue
blocks.info: A tissue consists of a collection of similar cells that collaborate to perform one or more specialized functions.

blocks.name: Organ
blocks.info: An organ is a distinct, structured assembly of tissues that function together to perform specific roles within the body.

blocks.name: System
blocks.info: A system is a collection of interconnected and interdependent organs that collaborate to achieve a particular function or set of functions.

segments.t: The human organism, the highest level of complexity, is an integrated structure comprising cells, tissues, organs, and systems. Each level is functionally interconnected and crucial for health, as any change in one part affects multiple processes or structures.

is the Ayurvedic principle of mobility that regulates all activity in the body and mind, from the flow of thoughts to the movement of food through the intestines. It is considered the most important dosha because it governs all biological movement and carries the other two doshas throughout the body. It is primarily composed of the Ether (Space) and Air elements.

items.t: Dry (
ruksha
): leading to dry skin, hair, and internal organs.
Light (
laghu
): manifesting as a thin body frame and scanty sleep.
Cold (
shita
): resulting in poor circulation and cold hands and feet.
Rough (
khara
): characterized by cracked skin, rough hair, and cracking joints.
Subtle (
sukshma
): associated with subtle fears and minute muscle tremors.
Mobile (
chala
): leading to fast walking, talking, and restlessness.
Clear (
vishada
): clarity of understanding, but also a sense of emptiness or isolation.

segments.t: ) of a Vāta individual is typically:

items.t: Body Frame: thin, slender, often disproportionate; very tall or very short, with visible bones and prominent veins.
Weight: generally low or underweight, with difficulty gaining weight.
Face: thin, angular, or oblong.
Nose: often thin, crooked, or uneven, and may have a deviated septum.
Eyes: small, sunken, dry, and active; the gaze is unsteady or darting. The iris is dark, gray, or brown.
Lips: thin, dry, and scaly, often with a brownish tinge.
Teeth: large, protruding, or irregular, with gaps between them.
Skin: thin, dry, cold to the touch, and rough; tends to a darker complexion and tans easily.
Hair: dry, brittle, curly or kinky; thin or scarce and prone to split ends and dandruff.
Nails: dry, brittle, rough, and break easily; may have grooves.
Appetite and Digestion: variable (
Vishama Agni
); ravenous one moment, not hungry the next. Digestion is irregular, with gas, bloating, and a tendency to constipation.
Sleep: scanty and interrupted; light sleepers, especially in cold or noisy places.
Speech: fast, spontaneous, sometimes slurred or disorganized.
Psychology: when balanced, creative, joyful, and flexible. When imbalanced, prone to fear, anxiety, insecurity, restlessness, and indecision.
Pulse: felt best under the index finger, moving like a serpent or cobra (
Sarpa
)—fast, feeble, cold, and thin.
Dreams: active and frequent, often of falling, flying, or being attacked.

segments.t: is the Ayurvedic principle of transformation that regulates metabolism, digestion, and the conversion of energy throughout the body and mind. Primarily composed of the Fire and Water elements, it manifests as the heat and biochemical actions required for life.

items.t: Hot (
ushna
): a higher body temperature, strong digestive fire, and intolerance for heat.
Sharp (
tikshna
): a sharp intellect, penetrating eyes, and pointed teeth.
Light (
laghu
): a medium body frame and light-headedness if meals are missed.
Liquid (
drava
): excess sweat, frequent urination, and loose stools.
Oily (
snigdha
): soft, oily skin and hair.
Spreading (
saram
): rashes or inflammation that spread across the body.
Fleshy smell (
visra
): a sulfuric or fetid body odor, particularly in the armpits.

segments.t: ) of a Pitta individual is generally balanced and moderate:

items.t: Body Frame: medium and well-proportioned, with good musculature and moderate strength.
Weight: moderate and stable; seldom gains or loses much.
Face: often heart-shaped, tapering, or triangular, with rosy or reddish cheeks.
Nose: medium-sized, sharp, and straight, often with a reddish tip.
Eyes: moderate, bright, and sharp; light-colored iris (gray, green, hazel, or yellowish), sensitive to light.
Lips: soft, thin, and pinkish or reddish.
Teeth: medium-sized, often yellowish or sharp; gums tender and prone to bleeding.
Skin: warm, oily, and sensitive; fair with a coppery or reddish complexion, prone to freckles, moles, acne, and sunburn.
Hair: straight, fine, and oily; soft brown, blond, or reddish, prone to premature graying or balding.
Nails: pink, flexible, lustrous, and sharp.
Appetite and Digestion: very strong and intense (
Tikshna Agni
); they become irritable if they do not eat on time. Digestion is fast but can cause heartburn or acid reflux.
Sleep: sound but moderate; may wake near midnight or 2 AM with a burst of energy.
Speech: sharp, clear, distinct, and often authoritative or inspiring.
Psychology: when balanced, intelligent, disciplined, and courageous leaders. When imbalanced, prone to anger, irritability, jealousy, judgment, and perfectionism.
Pulse: felt best under the middle finger, moving like a frog (
Manduka
)—jumping, bounding, hot, and forceful.
Dreams: fiery or intellectual—problem-solving, teaching, exams, fire, or violence.

segments.t: is the Ayurvedic principle of structure and lubrication that gives the body physical form, cohesion, and stability. It is the “glue” that holds the cells together and supplies the water for all bodily systems and joints. It is primarily composed of the Water and Earth elements.

items.t: Heavy (
guru
): heavy bones and muscles and a tendency toward being overweight.
Slow/Dull (
manda
): slow movement and sluggish metabolic changes.
Cold (
shita
): cool, clammy skin and slow digestion.
Oily (
snigdha
): oily skin and hair and lubricated joints.
Smooth (
shlakshna
): smoothness of the skin and organs.
Dense (
sandra
): a thickset body and compact tissues.
Soft (
mrudu
): soft skin and a gentle, caring personality.
Stable (
sthira
): stability and a preference for sedentary activities.
Sticky (
picchila
): cohesiveness, but also fogginess of the mind when imbalanced.
Gross (
sthula
): visible structures and the potential for obesity.

segments.t: ) of a Kapha individual is typically large and well-developed:

items.t: Body Frame: big, broad, and strong, with a large skeletal structure.
Weight: generally heavy; gains weight easily and finds it hard to lose.
Face: large, round, and attractive, with a “moon-shaped” look and plump cheeks.
Nose: large, wide, and thick; may be short and button-like.
Eyes: big, round, and beautiful, with long, thick lashes; iris blue, light gray, or black; very white sclera.
Lips: large, full, soft, and oily, often pale.
Teeth: large, strong, and white, regularly spaced, with strong gums.
Skin: thick, cool, soft, and oily; fair or pale, ages slowly and looks younger than its age.
Hair: thick, luxuriant, wavy, and oily; abundant and healthy even in old age.
Nails: strong, thick, smooth, and symmetrical, with a polished look.
Appetite and Digestion: slow but steady (
Manda Agni
); digestion is prolonged, with a feeling of heaviness or fullness.
Sleep: deep, sound, and prolonged; falls asleep easily and is hard to wake.
Speech: slow, melodious, and monotonous, with a deep, voluminous voice.
Psychology: when balanced, loving, compassionate, and forgiving. When imbalanced, prone to greed, attachment, possessiveness, and lethargy.
Pulse: felt best under the ring finger, moving like a swan (
Hamsa
)—slow, deep, and wavy.
Dreams: romantic and watery—lakes, oceans, swimming, snow, or ducks.
